scope: Scarlet Invocation Act signature moves: CinderCurtain (17, Act I), ShroudRope (18, Act II) and FourHands (19, Act III) replace the four basic notes of every third phrase (serial % 3 == 0) of Acts I-III; the seal crossflow stays the fifth note and Final is unchanged. Geometry lives in the Terraria-free CrimsonSignatureMoves and is shared by forecast, drawing and native collision. Damage stays at the rehearsal 1. No motions or new art
target_build: 0.3.69 / protocol79 (feat/scarlet-signature-moves, stacked on feat/scarlet-music-grid; protocol 78 is the music-grid integration)
design: lead design .local/design/signature-moves.md (2026-10-02), revised three times after review

fairness_model.forecast: one beat (28 ticks); the player reacts only to forecasts that are already visible (Born <= t) and may plan ahead only from what is shown
fairness_model.base: horizontal 0.08 px/tick^2 up to 3 px/tick (Terraria's run, about 35 px from rest in one beat); vertical gravity 0.4 (fall at most 10) and Lerp(vy, -12, .18) while jump is held
fairness_model.endgame: horizontal 0.2 px/tick^2 up to 6 px/tick (typical hardmode wings)
fairness_model.field_flight: CrimsonFieldPlayer refills wingTime every tick and gives wingless players the lift above, so everyone can fly indefinitely; a held full jump peaks around 130 px and hovering high is never a plan, which is why the rope has no permanently safe height
fairness_model.applies: CinderCurtain and ShroudRope are checked under BASE; FourHands assumes ENDGAME horizontal mobility like the basic beams (r 36)

implementation_decisions.four_hands_pair_order: the design's list {0,2} {1,3} {0,3} {1,2} leaves the safe quarters of beats 0/1 and 2/3 disjoint, contradicting its own rule that consecutive beats share a safe quarter. The same four pairs are ordered {0,2} {0,3} {1,3} {1,2} (safe {1,3} {1,2} {0,2} {0,3}); rotation by serial/3 % 4 is a label bijection so the rule holds for every rotation
implementation_decisions.four_hands_fingers: review change: a solid 646 px slab needed about 330 px of running from its middle within one forecast, so the claws became upright fingers (radius 110 -> 75 -> 60, spacing 213). Gaps are 93 px inside a quarter, 94 px across a quarter boundary and 47 px against a field wall; any sideways hook would cross the quarter edge or close a gap. Radius 60 because from the middle of a finger a body has to move 71 px (70 touching), which BASE cannot do in a beat but ENDGAME can
implementation_decisions.shroud_rope_staff: review change: the single low/high cut let anyone hover above the high cut, because the field gives everyone infinite flight. ShroudRope (ID kept) is now a five-line staff: even notes use a lower comb, odd notes a comb 112 px higher, both 224 px apart within a comb, lines running full width from alternating sides. The brief asked for centres 26/250/474/698/922 and 138/362/586/810/1034 with radius 24; those leave a 22 px window between every pair of neighbouring lines that is safe on both beats (a 42 px body fits the 64 px gap), and an 8 px sliver pinned to the ceiling. Radius 36 (the basic beams' radius) shrinks the neighbour gap to 40 px, below the body, and shifting the combs up 10 px (36/260/484/708/932 and 148/372/596/820/1044) lets the first line rest on the floor surface and the top line reach the ceiling, so no height at all stays safe on both beats. Cost: the farthest move between beats grows from 45 to 57 px (112.5 px from the ceiling, the one band with a single neighbour)
implementation_decisions.cinder_curtain_corridor: review change: the corridor is four columns (1,024 px) with one column of forward margin. A right walk is [o-2..o+1] [o-1..o+2] [o..o+3] [o+1..o+4], a left walk [o-1..o+2] [o-2..o+1] [o-3..o] [o-4..o-1]; right on even ordinals (serial / 3), left on odd, the other way when the preferred walk does not fit corridors 0..6. For o = 0, 1, 8, 9 neither fits and each note's corridor is clamped toward the nearer wall, so it slides in and stays ([0..3] on all notes for columns 0/1, [6..9] for 8/9). At most six columns burn
implementation_decisions.cinder_curtain_crowd: a forecast lasts one beat, so a member who is not the aimed one could be ~1,800 px from a single corridor. Every eligible member gets their own: Target carries the occupied-column mask (exact integer 1..1023, Y = 0, validated strictly; previously the aimed member's position), the safe columns of a note are the union of the per-member corridors, and the rest burn. A solo mask is stroke-for-stroke the single-corridor curtain; the full mask is accepted even if it leaves nothing burning. The client impact point for a curtain is the burning column nearest the local player, and a note with no burning column has no cue, shake or embers
implementation_decisions.cinder_curtain_join: a burning column beside a safe column keeps radius 128 so a corridor is never narrowed; other burning columns use 130 so they overlap their burning neighbours by 2 px
implementation_decisions.reach_ticks: curtain and hands fall over 3 ticks (smoothstep), the rope enters over 2 ticks like the spatial cuts; reach 0 emits no stroke; radii stay constant for the whole live window (no end taper)
implementation_decisions.unaimed_target: ShroudRope and FourHands carry the field centre in Target like ChoirRakes; CinderCurtain carries the occupied-column mask in all four notes (Target is not a place for it, so the client never uses it as one)
implementation_decisions.validation: signature techniques require Pulse < 4 and a live window of at most 20/12/16 ticks in CrimsonGesturePlan.Validate; a curtain's Target must be an exact integer 1..1023 with Y = 0
implementation_decisions.sounds: existing beam cue mapping; the rope uses the slash cues (ChargeLock/ChargeRush), the curtain and hands the default PortalFire

measured_properties.curtain_corridor: exactly 1,024 px free (scanned at 0.25 px steps at three heights for all seven corridor positions on two fields); every other point burns; 20x42 bodies fit anywhere in the corridor and one pixel into either wall burns
measured_properties.curtain_walk: one column per beat in one direction away from the member's column; the member's column is free for notes 0-2 at columns 2-7 and for all four notes against a wall (columns 0, 1, 8, 9, where the corridor stays put); consecutive corridors overlap by three columns inside the field and four against a wall; live windows (20 ticks) end before the next fall (28-29 ticks)
measured_properties.curtain_base_mobility: simulated per tick from rest under BASE (0.08 px/tick^2, 3 px/tick): interior columns 2-7 survive when they start running with the walk at note 1's warning, keeping at least 74 px of clearance from any burning column, and can be up to 74 px behind the column centre at that moment; wall columns survive standing still; a 90 px drift forward or back during the 30-tick look-ahead survives note 0 in every column
measured_properties.curtain_crowd: for all 1,023 masks and four phrases the production union equals an independently written one, every member's whole corridor is safe, at most six columns burn and no more strokes than the budget; for 160 masks (each single column, the full mask and pseudo-random crowds) the burning columns are exactly those outside every corridor, bodies fit every safe column and straddle safe neighbours, and a burning column beside a safe one keeps radius 128 (130 elsewhere); members still survive the BASE walk with other members around
measured_properties.rope_staff: five lines per note at 36/260/484/708/932 (even) and 148/372/596/820/1044 (odd) px above the floor, radius 36, all inside the 1,120 px field; a grounded body is hit on even beats and safe on odd beats; no height from 0 to 1,078 px is safe on both beats (checked at 0.5 px); the farthest a body has to move to change beat is 112.5 px from the ceiling (measured), 72 px from standing on the floor and 57 px from the middle of any other band (from the band widths); exhaustive search over jump held or released each tick (base flight) from 174 starting heights finds a way to the other beat's safe height within the 28-tick beat, and from the ceiling it needs 24 of the 28 ticks (14 ticks do not suffice)
measured_properties.hands_geometry: two quarters slammed per note, every quarter slammed twice and spared twice per phrase, consecutive beats share a safe quarter in every rotation; each slammed quarter is three upright fingers of radius 60 with 93 px gaps (94 px across a quarter boundary, 47 px against a wall), all within the quarter and 47 px from its edges; every gap takes a 20x42 body with 36 px each side; from any x along the floor the nearest clear standing spot is at most 71 px away on the 1 px grid (70 touching); safe quarters take a body anywhere 8 px inside their edges
measured_properties.hands_mobility: simulated per tick from rest at the note's warning, heading for the best gap and braking in it, against the real strokes: under ENDGAME (0.2 px/tick^2, 6 px/tick) every start clears the fingers, the smallest clearance over the live window being 12.4 px (worst start 2,455 px from the field's left edge); under BASE it does not (smallest -27.8 px, i.e. hit, worst start 950 px from the left edge). Four Hands therefore assumes endgame horizontal mobility, like the basic beams

checks.domain: passed: every new and changed case (selection cadence 3/6/9/12 and IDs, curtain corridor, walk, BASE-mobility survival, crowd union against an independent oracle, rope staff geometry and reachability, hands quarters, fingers and ENDGAME/BASE mobility, mask and descriptor codecs and rejections); mutating the corridor margin, rope radius, finger radius or crowd union makes the cases fail
checks.python: passed: tools/tests, including the wiring check for the shared geometry and the single curtain observation of every eligible member
checks.native_build: passed: tools/dev.py build --native into an isolated profile, tML 2026.08.3.0, 0 errors / 4 existing warnings
checks.offline_plots: passed: .local/geometry-preview (not committed) links the production domain sources and rasterises CrimsonTechniqueGeometry.Write through CrimsonTechniqueGeometry.Intersects; inspected the right-walking, left-walking, wall and crowd curtains with four-column corridors, the five-line staff on an even and an odd beat with bodies at seven heights, and all four rotations of the fingered hands. Shapes, corridors, free and hit bodies matched the model. These are geometry plots, not the production materials

not_run: in-game play of any signature move, including the feel of the walking corridor, the staff's up/down rhythm with a real jump and flight, and the finger gaps at endgame speed
readability of the soft forecast bands over the sanctum and against the existing live material (another branch is replacing the live material)
